title: Hearing Major and Minor
description: Tell a major chord from a minor one by sound alone. No keys, just ears.

steps.title: Bright or dark
steps.description:
Major chords tend to sound bright and settled. Minor chords sound darker, a bit more serious. The only difference between them is one middle note, a single key apart, but your ear picks it up fast.

You'll hear a few chords. Don't overthink it. Go with your first impression.

steps.title: First chord
steps.description: Listen to this one. Does it sound major or minor?
steps.hint: Does it feel open and sunny, or a little cloudy?

steps.title: Same root, new chord
steps.description: Same bottom note as before, but something has changed. Major or minor?
steps.hint: Play the last one back in your head and compare. Brighter or darker?

steps.title: A chord on D
steps.description: This one's built on D. Is it major or minor?
steps.hint: Try humming the middle note. Does it feel like it's lifting or sinking?

steps.title: A chord on E
steps.description: Now one built on E. Major or minor?

steps.title: A chord on A
steps.description: This one sits a little lower. What do you hear?

steps.title: Last one, on F
steps.description: One more, built on F. Major or minor?
